paras: Rails of Time is an inter-university project reflecting a new form of innovative educational engineering based on design thinking.

The project title plays on words: "Rails of Time" refers both to a real itinerary and to a metaphorical link between generations, cultures, and traditions across time. By traveling through different French cities, participants discover cultural traces of the past and present while exploring the living stories of those whose creativity shapes territories.

The project takes the form of a new-generation travelogue in which students design itineraries, produce short films, conduct interviews, and write research narratives while immersing themselves in local culture, innovation, and creative practices.

items.p: Turn students’ coursework into real fieldwork with France’s territories, companies and local actors.
Build interviewing, filmmaking and intercultural skills by documenting real local “heroes.”
Show how communities and businesses of every size drive cultural, economic and ecological change.
Have Generation U students mentor younger pupils and share their work with the public.

outline.lede: The project unfolds in several complementary phases designed as a progressive path of transmission, creation, and intergenerational dialogue.

phases.label: Phase 1
phases.p: Rails of Time – Generation U is the first stage of the project. It is designed for students from partner higher education institutions and is integrated into their academic curriculum.
phases.quote: Local companies and personalities become the "heroes" of the films created by students and the subjects of academic analysis.

phases.label: Phase 2
phases.p: Rails of Time – Junior is based on an intergenerational transmission approach. Higher education students become tutors and mediators, guiding middle and high school students throughout the project.

cta.p: Join our creative and educational projects. Contact us to learn more about partnership opportunities.

hero.lede: The meeting of cultures is a spark capable of transforming the world within us and around us.

paras: ASSO S.L.A.V.É. is an intellectual laboratory bringing together people from diverse backgrounds around creative, educational, and sustainable projects.

The association's main activity is the development of projects at the intersection of science, entrepreneurship, culture, art, sustainable development, and technology. Particular attention is given to cinema, digital media, and artificial intelligence, as well as to traditional artistic practices, as tools for intercultural exchange and responsible development.
about.caption: The S.L.A.V.É. team — Bordeaux

history.title: History & Values
history.hint: Founded in 2007 at Université Bordeaux Montaigne. How the association got here.
paras: The association was founded in 2007 at Université Bordeaux Montaigne by students and professors passionate about cultural dialogue with Eastern Europe, former USSR countries, and the Slavic world.

From the beginning, the association stood out through the organization of numerous cultural and scientific events led by professionals from the economic, academic, and artistic worlds. One of its most emblematic projects was the international short film competition In Ciné Veritas.

Over time, the association has evolved, structured, and expanded its activities by developing educational workshops in various academic fields such as communication, management, entrepreneurship, art, creative industries, and marketing. It also conducts oral and written translation activities aligned with its original academic expertise.

These actions rely on research-action methods and design thinking approaches and extend into creative projects, the design of tourism routes in France and Europe, and the promotion of territories and their economic actors, regardless of size.

The association is also committed to inclusivity and respect for human dignity by developing projects that promote access to culture, education, and creativity for diverse audiences, while valuing participation, autonomy, and self-expression as drivers of responsible and sustainable development.
Through this evolution, the association has moved beyond its initial scope to become an interdisciplinary, territorial, and European platform.
Faithful to its academic roots and philosophy—education, culture, and art as tools for transformation—the association has become an intercultural, intergenerational, and interdisciplinary platform.

pillars.lede: Five fields through which the association brings cultures together.

items.p: Educational workshops and academic projects — from management and entrepreneurship to applied linguistics, AI and the creative industries.
Translation, interpretation and intercultural mediation that bring people, institutions and cultures together.
Cinema, digital media and audiovisual creation, with a special focus on film and new technologies.
Cultural and tourism itineraries that reveal the people and places shaping France’s territories.
Mobility, inclusion and exchange — connecting diverse people and communities through shared experience.

featured.lede: Two flagship initiatives where culture, education and solidarity meet.

items.p: An intercultural and educational journey across France — students design routes, make short documentary films and tell the living stories of the people shaping local territories.
Social action and intercultural support for people and families — translation, guidance, community connection and solidarity that uphold the dignity of everyone we work with.

hero.lede: The association develops concrete actions and sustainable projects to guarantee the dignity of individuals, especially those in vulnerable situations.

items.p: Concrete support for elders, children, families and women facing hardship.
Guide newcomers through administrative, legal and medical steps — with translation and interpretation.
Link generations through workshops, shared activities and a community library.
Help with respect for privacy and dignity, never replacing qualified professionals.

areas.lede: Recurring, one-time, and field actions to support those in need

bullets: Help with moving within the care facility

imgs.alt: Support for Children with Specific Needs or Affected by Illness

bullets: Support for family projects and initiatives
Books on life in France, social rights, health, and more
A space for exchange and continuous learning

furniture.lede: Light repairs and restoration of furniture for elderly residents — a concrete example of our commitment to dignity and care.

items.p: Developing cooperation between young volunteers and elderly people through shared activities.
Building tailored career paths for people in professional transition.
bullets: Adapted career paths (e.g., PE teacher turned tiler, foreign diploma validation via ENIC-NARIC)
CV and cover letter writing workshops
Connection with training centers (AFPA, CNAM) and integration structures

paras: Our actions rely on the commitment of volunteers and take place within a punctual and time-limited framework.
We support individuals in their procedures (translation, guidance) and help them in the design and development of their projects.
The association operates within the limits of its skills and resources, without substituting for qualified professionals (legal, medical, or social).
We also ensure strict respect for the limits of our intervention, as well as the privacy and autonomy of the people we support.

cta.p: Join our actions for dignity. Whether as a volunteer, partner, or donor, every contribution makes a difference in the lives of vulnerable people.
